clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old girl presented with 3 weeks of right-sided headache and horizontal binocular diplopia, initially diagnosed as right cranial nerve VI palsy. Initial brain MRI was normal, and symptoms persisted despite initial treatments. Extensive workup, including normal CBC, electrolytes, chest X-ray, CSF studies (normal cell count, no malignant cells, normal PCR, culture, α-fetoprotein, oligoclonal bands, ACE), and serological tests (normal SPEP, ANA, ANCA, anti-dsDNA, etc.), ruled out infectious, neoplastic, and other inflammatory/autoimmune causes. MRA and MRV were normal, ruling out cavernous sinus thrombosis. A repeat MRI brain and orbits, performed 11 days after the first, revealed a possible cavernous sinus lesion. Following multidisciplinary discussion, the patient received high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, which led to noted improvements in her headaches, diplopia, and right eye abduction. The diagnosis of an idiopathic inflammatory process, Tolosa-Hunt syndrome, was concluded based on the exclusion of other causes and the positive response to corticosteroids.
